name: January 25, 2025 Palisades Fire Town Hall and Community Forum Special Meeting
agenda_text:
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: The meeting will be live streamed at www.malibucity.org/video.

  HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
  submit correspondence and questions to forms.office.com/r/8CBV4EmFf7 before the meeting begins.

  HOW TO PARTICIPATE IN-PERSON DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may
  speak during the meeting in-person.

  Malibu City Council
  Palisades Fire Town Hall and Community Forum
  Special Meeting Agenda

  Saturday, January 25, 2025
  4:00 P.M. – CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING
  Malibu High School Auditorium
  30215 Morning View Drive

To the members of the City Council of the City of Malibu:

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a Special Meeting of the City Council of the City of
Malibu to be held at the Malibu High School Auditorium, 30215 Morning View Drive, Malibu, CA 90265, at
4:00 p.m. on Saturday, January 25, 2025, for the purpose of holding a town hall meeting regarding the Palisades
Fire.

Four p.m.  Palisades Fire Town Hall Community Forum

  The City of Malibu and representatives from partner agencies will host a Town Hall and
  Community Forum to hear directly from the residents about the Palisades Fire and answer
  questions about fire response and recovery.

  Staff Contact: Deputy City Manager Brown, 456-2489, ext. 300

Adjournment

  Guide to the City Council Proceedings and Decorum

 Role of the Presiding Officer: The presiding officer of the City Council, who shall be the Mayor, shall be responsible
 for maintaining the order and decorum of meetings. It shall be the duty of the presiding officer to ensure that these rules
 of procedure and decorum are followed at all times. The presiding officer shall maintain control of communication
 between Councilmembers, between the Council and the public, and chair each meeting in a fair and impartial manner. It
 shall be the duty of each Councilmember to support the presiding officer in maintaining the order and decorum of Council
 meetings.

 Members of the Audience: Members of the audience shall not engage in disorderly or boisterous conduct, including
 clapping, whistling, stamping of feet, or other acts which disturb, disrupt, impede or otherwise disturb the orderly conduct
 of the City Council meeting. Persons addressing the City Council shall not engage in disorderly conduct which disrupts,
 City Council Special Meeting Agenda  Page - 2 -  January 25, 2025

  or otherwise impedes the orderly conduct or Council meetings. Any person who so disrupts a Council meeting may, at
  the discretion of the presiding officer or a majority of the City Council, be subject to ejection from that meeting.

  City Council meetings are aired live and replayed on City of Malibu Government Access Channel 3 and are
  available on demand on the City’s website at www.malibucity.org/video. Copies of the staff reports or other written
  documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the office of the City Clerk and available
  upon request by emailing cityclerk@malibucity.org.

  The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
  please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans
  with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Environmental
  Sustainability Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable
  the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title
  II].

  I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
  in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Special meeting agendas may be amended up to 24 hours in
  advance of the meeting. Dated this 21st day of January 2025 at 7:45 p.m.

  Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk

MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
F“  SPECIAL MEETING
  PALISADES FIRE TOWN HALL AND COMMUNITY FORUM
  JANUARY 25, 2025
  MALIBU HIGH SCHOOL AUDITORIUM
  4:00 P.M.

  MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Deputy City Manager explained ground rules for public participation and how the meeting
  would be conducted.

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 4:04 pm.

  Los Angeles County Fire representatives provided an updated on the Palisades Fire and
  discussed the response to the fire, damage inspections, and repopulation plans.

  Romuald Jovero, Small Business Association, discussed resources for homeowners and
  renters, including loans and grants.

  Tara Fitzgerald, Environmental Protection Agency, discussed fire debris removal.

  Brandon Monson, FEMA, discussed its role in response to disasters and resources to
  support recovery.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.
  ‘ ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Acting City
  Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability
  Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning Director; Susan Dueflas, Public Safety
  Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Cynthia Alba, Executive Assistant; Parker
  Davis, Media Technician; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Tracey Rossine,
  Environmental Programs Manager; and Travis Hart, Deputy Public Works Director

  PANELISTS: Congressman Brad Sherman, 32nd US Congressional District; Senator Ben
  Allen, 24th District, CA State Senate; Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin, 42nd District CA
  State Assembly; Supervisor Lindsey Horvath, 3rd District, County of Los Angeles Board
  of Supervisors; Environmental Protection Agency ; FEMA; US Army Corp of Engineers;
  Small Business Administration; CalOES; California Coastal Commission; Los Angeles
  County Sheriff Department; Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District; Los Angeles
  County Public Works; Los Angeles County Waterworks District 29; SoCal Gas; Southern
  California Edison; CalFire; and Los Angeles County Fire Department
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 25, 2025
  Page 2 of 2

  PALISADES FIRE TOWN HALL AND COMMUNITY FORUM

  Mayor Stewart open the Q&A and announced the public comment would be limited to a
  minute and a half per speaker.

  The panelists answered questions and heard comments regarding:

  Debris removal and opting in or out of the debris removal program, mudslides risks,
  repopulation, repairing damaged infrastructure, timeline for rebuilding, Mountains
  Recreation Conservation Authority’s land managements, defensible space, fire response
  and Fire Department resources, waterworks system capacities, undergrounding and
  hardening electrical systems, fire rebuild permitting, property taxes, Pacific Coast
  Highway access, Public Safety Power Shutoff'impacts, insurance, problems with the
  emergency notification system, home hardening for f1re defense, staffing at City Hall,
  avoiding scams, continuity of education through disasters, resources for those impacted by
  the Franklin Fire in December 2024, experiences evacuation from the Palisades Fire,
  temporary housing during rebuilding, and residents’ experiences fighting the Palisades
  Fire.

  ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Stewart adjourned the meeting at 8:23 pm
